title: Claude-compat managed-settings.json (Grok Build consumed subset)
description: Describes ONLY the subset of Claude Code's vendor `managed-settings.json` (MDM/IT-administered policy file) keys that Grok Build (this codebase) actually reads. This is NOT the full Claude Code managed-settings schema; real managed-settings.json files may contain additional keys Grok Build ignores, so additionalProperties is never false anywhere in this schema. Platform paths: macOS `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json`, Linux `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json`. Supported surface today is a SINGLE file at that path; grok does NOT yet merge Claude's `managed-settings.d/` drop-ins, an MDM plist, or Windows registry delivery. `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` from this file is deliberately NOT consulted for grok's own always-approve lock (grok must not inherit a host-wide Claude lockdown from this file); grok still honors this file's permission rules, MCP allow/deny lists, and marketplace allowlist. To hard-lock always-approve in grok itself, use a root-owned requirements.toml instead.

env.description: Only two keys are read; both are read via a tolerant boolean coercion (json_env_flag): a JSON number is truthy iff nonzero, a JSON bool is used as-is, a JSON string is false for "0"/""/"false" and true for anything else, any other JSON type (array/object/null) yields no value (key ignored, not an error).

DISABLE_TELEMETRY.description: Disables telemetry collection when truthy. Coerced via json_env_flag: a number is truthy iff nonzero, a boolean is used as-is, a string is false for "0"/""/"false" and true otherwise.

DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND.description: Disables the feedback command when truthy. Coerced via json_env_flag: a number is truthy iff nonzero, a boolean is used as-is, a string is false for "0"/""/"false" and true otherwise.

permissions.description: Parsed via a STRICT (non-tolerant) serde deserialize of {allow, deny, ask} -- unlike the project-tier `.claude/settings.json` (which tolerantly skips individual malformed array entries), a single wrong-typed entry anywhere in `allow`/`deny`/`ask` fails deserialization of the WHOLE `permissions` object, silently dropping ALL permission rules from this file (still not a file-load error).

allow.description: Permission-rule strings, action=Allow. Part of the strict {allow, deny, ask} deserialize -- see the parent `permissions` description.

deny.description: Permission-rule strings, action=Deny. Part of the strict {allow, deny, ask} deserialize -- see the parent `permissions` description.

ask.description: Permission-rule strings, action=Ask. Part of the strict {allow, deny, ask} deserialize -- see the parent `permissions` description.

defaultMode.description: Highest-precedence permission-mode source (overrides user-tier files). Shares the same extraction helper as project-tier settings.json: if present but not a string, the value is ignored.

disableBypassPermissionsMode.description: Compared against the literal string "disable" (any other value, including a non-string JSON type, resolves to false rather than an error). Feeds `ManagedSettingsFeatures::disable_yolo`, which is READ but NOT used to hard-lock grok's own always-approve mode (see top-level description).

allowedMcpServers.description: MCP server allowlist. Deny takes precedence over allow (deny-wins semantics).

deniedMcpServers.description: MCP server denylist. An entry matching none of serverUrl/command/serverName is logged as an ignored/unsupported entry (allow-side entries fail silently instead, since an ungranted entry is fail-closed).

items.description: Only entries with `source == "git"` AND a present `url` are loaded into the in-memory marketplace allowlist; entries with any other `source` value, or a `git` entry missing `url`, are silently dropped from the allowlist (not a validation failure of the document).

strictKnownMarketplaces.description: Marketplace allowlist: when non-empty, only git marketplace sources whose URL matches an entry here are permitted. Only entries with `source == "git"` and a present `url` contribute to the allowlist; other entries are silently dropped (see item description).

McpServerPolicyEntry.description: Matched in this order against a single JSON object: `serverUrl` (string) -> Http, else `command` (string) -> Stdio, else `serverName` (string) -> Name (match by config name, any transport). The three keys are not mutually exclusive in the schema (grok only inspects them in this priority order; extra sibling keys don't invalidate the entry).
